ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy second set with monster jam from He's Gone to China Doll
ai_show_review.blurb: The February 19, 1973 International Amphitheatre show delivers a seamless, high‑octane second set that strings together He's Gone → Truckin' → The Other One → Eyes Of The World → China Doll. Jerry's guitar shines on the ballad ending, Phil lays down lead‑bass lines throughout, and Bill's cymbals add extra sparkle. Excellent soundboard recordings capture every nuance of this standout performance.
ai_show_review.review: The Dead’s February 19, 1973 gig at Chicago’s International Amphitheatre is a textbook example of early‑’73 second‑set brilliance. After a concise first set, the band launches into an almost hour‑long improvisational marathon that begins with a fiery He's Gone and rolls straight into a soaring Truckin'. From there The Other One erupts into a deep, exploratory jam before giving way to an expansive Eyes Of The World that morphs beautifully into a tender China Doll—where Jerry’s tone is described as flawless. The set closes with the usual high‑octane pair of Sugar Magnolia and Casey Jones, leaving the audience buzzing. Across three soundboard sources the performance is consistently praised; the Miller capture stands out for its crystal‑clear mix and lack of drop‑outs, making it the definitive listen. Phil’s “lead‑bass” work shines all night, while Bill Kreutzmann’s cymbal crashes add a shimmering edge to the jams. Keith’s keyboards provide subtle texture throughout, rounding out an ensemble that was truly in sync during this peak February show.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp, clean mix and no noticeable drop‑outs, preserving full band dynamics despite venue acoustics.
